_meta.description: FIFA World Cup 2026 venue weather and environmental conditions for match-day prediction adjustments.
sources: PMC study PMC11947059: Extreme heat risk and implications for FIFA World Cup 2026 scheduling
Climate Central: 2026 World Cup Stadiums heat analysis (climatecentral.org/climate-matters/world-cup-stadiums)
NOAA US Climate Normals — June/July averages for each host city
Wikipedia: 2026 FIFA World Cup host city climate sections

heatIndexScale.1: Mild — ≤22 °C avg match-day, low humidity. Minimal heat stress for any squad.
heatIndexScale.2: Moderate — 23–28 °C, manageable humidity. Small performance reduction for poorly-acclimatised squads.
heatIndexScale.3: High — 28–32 °C and/or >60 % humidity. Performance-impairing heat for cold-climate squads; FIFA hydration breaks apply.
heatIndexScale.4: Severe — 32–35 °C and/or >70 % humidity (open-air). Significant physiological stress; sprint volume and pressing intensity drop markedly.
heatIndexScale.5: Extreme — >35 °C combined with high humidity, or sustained heat above 33 °C with no climate control. Maximum heat stress; >80 % of June/July days exceed 28 °C WBGT threshold.

notes: heatIndex reflects outdoor ambient conditions during the June–July tournament window.
effectiveHeatIndex applies reductions for fully climate-controlled (AC dome) or retractable-roof venues where FIFA confirms indoor match conditions.
altitudeM > 1000 triggers an altitude modifier in the prediction engine. Teams with ≥30 % of squad from high-altitude club leagues receive a reduced altitude penalty.

eveningKickoffReduction: subtract this value from effectiveHeatIndex for kickoffs at or after 18:00 local time (evening matches are 2–4 °C cooler outdoors; FIFA mandates evening kickoffs in extreme-heat cities).
humidityPct figures are mid-afternoon averages; morning figures are 5–10 % higher.

Miami.notes: Hottest and most humid open-air WC venue. No shade, no AC. Morning humidity peaks at 86 %. Night matches only marginally cooler. Squads from cold/temperate European clubs face the largest physiological deficit here.

Monterrey.notes: Hottest dry-heat venue. Daytime highs regularly 36–38 °C in July. Humidity lower than Miami but radiant heat on pitch is severe. Evening kickoffs scheduled by FIFA provide some relief. Low altitude (538 m) is negligible.

Houston.notes: Outdoor conditions are extreme (34 °C, ~77 % humidity) but NRG Stadium's retractable roof will be closed and AC active for all matches — FIFA confirmed. Match-day interior conditions reduce effective heat stress by ~1–1.5 tiers. Travel, warm-ups and pre-match exposure still subject to outdoor conditions.

Dallas.notes: Outdoor July highs average 38 °C — hottest raw temperature of any WC venue. However low humidity (54 %) and AT&T Stadium's AC roof significantly reduce match-day conditions. Indoor effective heat index estimated at tier 3. Evening kickoffs outdoors still very hot.

Kansas City.notes: Open-air. Significant heat especially in afternoon; evening matches considerably cooler. ~55 % of June/July days exceed 28 °C WBGT. Humidity moderate. Cold-climate European squads will feel the heat, though less than Miami/Monterrey.

Atlanta.heatRisk: High (mitigated by fully enclosed AC dome)
Atlanta.notes: Mercedes-Benz Stadium is a fully enclosed fixed dome with central HVAC — the most climate-controlled of all WC 2026 venues. Match-day conditions expected to be near-neutral (effective tier 2). Outdoor Atlanta in July is hot and humid, but players spend minimal time in outdoor conditions.

Philadelphia.notes: Open-air stadium. June/July sees warm to hot conditions with moderate humidity. About 50 % of days exceed 28 °C WBGT threshold. Evening matches substantially more comfortable. Northern-European club squads will feel a moderate heat disadvantage.

Guadalajara.heatRisk: High (altitude is the dominant stressor here)
Guadalajara.notes: Temperatures are moderate compared to other venues (25–26 °C in rainy season). The primary stressor at Guadalajara is altitude (1,556 m): aerobic capacity drops ~6–8 % for non-adapted teams. Teams with players from high-altitude club cities (Bogotá, Quito, Medellín, Mexico City) receive reduced altitude penalty. Rainy season may produce afternoon showers.

New York.notes: Open-air venue in New Jersey. July can produce warm humid days, but conditions are well within the comfort zone of most squads. Final (July 19) expected to be evening kick-off with pleasant conditions. ~35 % of days reach performance-impairing WBGT levels.

Boston.notes: Located in Foxborough, Massachusetts. New England's maritime climate keeps June/July conditions mild to warm. Less than 30 % of days exceed WBGT 28 °C. One of the more comfortable open-air venues. Humidity can spike during heatwave periods.

Los Angeles.notes: SoFi Stadium has a translucent canopy roof with open sides; it is not a fully sealed AC environment but provides significant shade. Inglewood near the coast sees moderate temperatures and low humidity compared to inland LA. June mornings are often overcast (marine layer). Conditions are comfortable for most squads.

Toronto.notes: Toronto's Great Lakes climate keeps summers warm but rarely extreme. BMO Field is a smaller open-air stadium on the waterfront. Humidity can be noticeable but temperatures stay below 30 °C on most match days. Comfortable conditions for European-based squads.

Mexico City.heatRisk: Moderate heat — but HIGH ALTITUDE is the dominant stressor
Mexico City.notes: Estadio Azteca sits at 2,240 m above sea level — the highest WC 2026 venue. Temperatures are mild (18–20 °C in rainy season). Heat is almost not a factor. However, aerobic capacity drops 8–12 % at this altitude for non-adapted teams. Teams from Bogotá (2,640 m), Quito (2,850 m), or Mexico City domestic clubs are fully adapted. Thin air also affects ball aerodynamics (longer ball flight, unpredictable swerve). Rainy-season afternoon showers common.

San Francisco Bay Area.notes: Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara. Bay Area marine climate keeps temperatures mild year-round. June mornings are cool and overcast; afternoon highs rarely exceed 24 °C. The mildest heat conditions of any US venue. Any squad, regardless of climate background, performs near their baseline here. Occasional strong winds off the bay.

Seattle.notes: Pacific Northwest oceanic climate. June in Seattle averages 19 °C with mild humidity. Heat stress is essentially zero — fewer than 6 % of days approach WBGT 28 °C. Open-air but excellent natural ventilation. Neutral venue from a weather standpoint for every squad. One of the most equitable environments in the draw.

Vancouver.notes: BC Place has a retractable roof but June/July temperatures are so mild it will typically be open. Vancouver's marine climate is among the most temperate of any WC host city. Virtually no heat stress for any squad. Comfortable for European and South American squads alike. Evening temperatures drop further to 14–17 °C.

altitudeTierScale.0: Negligible (<600 m) — no altitude modifier applied.
altitudeTierScale.1: Minor (600–1200 m) — 0.5 pt penalty for both teams; adapted teams exempted.
altitudeTierScale.2: Moderate (1200–1800 m) — 1.5 pt penalty for both teams; adapted teams exempted.
altitudeTierScale.3: High (>1800 m) — 2.5 pt penalty for both teams; adapted teams receive 0 pt penalty.

heatAdjustmentFormula.description: Applied per-team inside predictInternationalFixture(). The diff between teams' adjustments shifts the match rating differential.

parameters.effectiveHeatIndex: From this file, per venue city. Reduced by eveningKickoffReduction if kickoff >= 18:00 local.
parameters.squadClimateScore: Weighted average climate tier of squad's club leagues (1=cold, 5=hot/humid). From squad_climate_profiles.json.

heatAdjustmentFormula.interpretation: A team with squadClimateScore 1.8 (Premier League-heavy) playing in Miami (effectiveHeatIndex 5): adj = -(5-1.8)*0.5 = -1.6 pts. A team with squadClimateScore 4.5 (Brazilian league) playing in Miami: adj = -(5-4.5)*0.5 = -0.25 pts. The difference (-1.6 vs -0.25) gives Brazil a net +1.35 rating edge solely from weather acclimatisation.
